items.author: TOI TECH DESK
items.description: Anthropic has priced its IPO at $83 per share, achieving a valuation of $1.5 trillion. This valuation exceeds the total market capitalization of India's top 10 companies by a significant margin. Uday Kotak of Kotak Mahindra Bank raised concerns about whether Indian firms are undervalued or need to improve in technology sectors. The company reported an impressive revenue of $33.2 billion for the first nine months of 2026.

items.title: Owl survives 65mph truck crash, travels 70 miles trapped in front before rescue
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: In an incredible tale of survival, a great horned owl in Pennsylvania endured a harrowing journey after being struck by a truck and wedged in its air dam. Traveling roughly 70 miles, the owl was finally found by trucking terminal employees. Despite sustaining an eye injury, it was otherwise unharmed.

items.title: LT Foods share price rockets 8% after subsidiary acquires US’ Maya Kaimal in $6 million deal
items.description: LT Foods shares rallied on Thursday after its US subsidiary acquired MK Food Holdings for $5.8 million. The deal adds Maya Kaimal, a premium Indian-inspired foods brand, to its portfolio. Known for its sauces, curries and rice products, the brand will strengthen LT Foods' ready-to-eat offerings and US presence.

items.title: Indian man found dead inside burning car in Canada, had 'limited known' contacts
items.author: AYUSH PANDEY
items.description: Tushar Sharma, a resident of Surrey, was discovered dead in a burning vehicle on October 29. Firefighters located human remains while extinguishing the fire in Langley, British Columbia. The Integrated Homicide Investigation Team is investigating the case for potential motives and contacts. Police believe Sharma was specifically targeted despite his limited criminal background and acquaintances. Investigators request public assistance with information and any related CCTV or dashcam footage.

items.title: Viking hoard with sword, brooches and scales found on Isle of Man now on display
items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: Daniel Crowe made an astonishing discovery of a Viking hoard on the Isle of Man, revealing a trove of jewellery and weapons that shed light on the social hierarchy and burial customs of the early Viking Age. This remarkable collection offers crucial insights into the roles women played in Viking society, with artefacts showcasing intricate designs and suggesting links to extensive trading networks across the British Isles.

items.title: New bluish-black scorpion found in Odisha's Similipal, first of genus in state
items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: A newly documented scorpion species has been unveiled, representing the first instance of Liocheles in Odisha. Researchers designated this species as Liocheles similipalensis following an in-depth analysis of its physical traits. With this addition, the total number of recognized Liocheles species globally rises to seven, and four of these have been discovered in India.

items.title: 'Ramayana' hits Rs 1,500 crore mark at box office in record time
items.author: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK
items.description: Namit Malhotra's 'Ramayana', directed by Nitesh Tiwari, has crossed the Rs 1,000 crore mark domestically. The film achieved this milestone within just two weeks of its theatrical release. Starring Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, and Sai Pallavi, it is now the sixth Indian film to reach this figure. In addition, 'Ramayana' has become the third Bollywood movie to join this exclusive club. Its worldwide gross collection currently stands at Rs 1,519.

items.title: Washington man denied parenthood after court finds pregnancy came from assault
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: A Washington court ruled against a man's request for legal fatherhood of a child conceived through sexual assault. The ruling was based on Washington's Uniform Parentage Act, which addresses situations involving sexual violence. The child's mother provided credible evidence of ongoing abuse and intimidation from the man throughout their relationship. While the man claimed the relationship was consensual, the court found his testimony inconsistent and unconvincing.

items.description: In 2011, Joe Demin and Rachel Connors embarked on a journey with Yellow Leaf Hammocks, originally as a side venture. Specializing in handwoven hammocks crafted by the Mlabri Tribe in Thailand, the couple faced a turning point during the pandemic. Post-Shark Tank, they pivoted to a direct-to-consumer model, empowering local women through training and crafting. Their dedication culminated in over $30 million in sales, profoundly impacting families.
